claim: The red fluorescent tracer particles are spherical polystyrene, surface-functionalised with carboxyl (-COOH) groups, supplied as a suspension in deionised water.

identifiers.applies_to: the Abvigen catalogue product, NOT the bottle in use

validity_conditions: Applies to the product family as supplied, at every diameter it is sold in, and says nothing about which diameter is in use here (gap tracer_diameter_unknown). WHY THIS IS AN ENTRY AND NOT FILING. Spherical and polystyrene are the two premises a Stokes-Einstein estimate rests on, and a caller that assumes them without a source has made an assumption it cannot cite; carboxyl surface is what governs whether the particles stick to glass or to each other, which is an imaging outcome and not chemistry trivia. THE REFRACTIVE INDEX IS NOT HERE. Polystyrene has a well-known one and this document does not print it, so nothing is entered for it from this source -- but the gap changes character: refractive_index was `absent` and is now findable, because the material is established and a real optical reference can be cited against it. Filling it from memory would be E6 and would enter nothing. NO SUBJECT, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. Check 44 resolves a `quantity` subject against the names actually used in numbers[] somewhere, and refused an earlier draft of this entry with the right instruction attached -- a subject names a registry so that it can be wrong, do not add the id to make this pass. There is no registry id for the tracer particle: `device` is drawn from the channels and elements of kb/staging/devices.v0.json and a sample is not hardware, `configuration` is an optical path, and contracts/observables.json holds two ids, neither of them this. So the field is left off rather than filled with something adjacent. This is the third instance of one structural gap, after `at` having nowhere to point for 'the room' (lab_ambient_temperature) and the per-lens handle in the pixel-size calibrations; it is raised with manager-librarian, who owns contracts/observables.json. THE PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION IS WITHDRAWN -- THIS ENTRY IS NOT ABOUT THE BOTTLE ON THIS BENCH. On 2026-09-19 the person ruled that AFR-0500-COOH is not what is in use. Two facts force it: the bottle's label does not state a product identity (bottle_label_states_no_product, E3, and it was LOOKED AT -- so this is permanent doubt, not doubt pending a look), and the particles in use fluoresce under green excitation and show through a 605 band (particles_show_on_the_green_605_path, E2), which a particle emitting at 680 nm as this data sheet specifies does not do. The observation was made on this bench and the specification was not; 10.3 rule 1 binds a vendor exactly as it binds a prior project. WHAT IS AND IS NOT RETRACTED. This entry remains TRUE ABOUT THE ABVIGEN PRODUCT. Nothing in the data sheet has been found wrong about the thing the data sheet describes. What is withdrawn is that the thing it describes is ours. It is kept rather than deleted under rule 8, and because the next person to find this sheet needs to meet the record that it was examined and set aside. THE QUERY HANDLES WERE RENAMED, AND THAT IS THE ACTUAL REPAIR. The numbers used to answer to names beginning `tracer_`, and the word `tracer` is the claim that these are ours -- asserted in a string that nothing validates. Check 44 refused the `subject` fields on these entries and they were removed rather than gamed, which left the name as the only handle, so the claim did not disappear when the check rejected it: it moved somewhere no check reaches. The names now begin `abvigen_`, so a query for our tracer no longer lands here. The entry_id still begins `tracer_` and is deliberately left alone: it is the citation handle, it is referenced by name from the polystyrene dispersion entries, and renaming it would be a deletion under rule 8.
